claim: D3: an erosion feeder in the raw bucket holds the dose between 1 and 5 mg/L for standing times of 30 minutes to a day
law: A release set by contact time gives dose proportional to standing time (TAMU tablet chlorination guide: dissolution depends on contact amount and time)
check: 48 ratio of longest to shortest standing time <= 5 ratio of longest to shortest standing time

claim: D3: left overnight at a rate that gives 2 mg/L in 30 min the bucket reaches about 96 mg/L
law: Dose = rate x time / volume; WHO guideline value 5 mg/L
check: Set instead for 5 mg/L at 24 h, the 30 minute dose is 0.10 mg/L, far below 0.5

claim: D3: TCCA pool tablets release chlorine slowly and safely in a wetted feeder
law: TAMU: TCCA not approved for tablet chlorinators, too slow, and repeated wetting can form explosive nitrogen trichloride; never mix with calcium hypochlorite
check: Hazard as well as range; calcium hypochlorite erosion feeders work only in flowing water

claim: D3: the household can see when the feeder is spent or over-dosing
law: No dose indication without a chlorine test
check: Fails: no dose indication without a chlorine test, so under- or over-dose is silent; the option is dropped on X1
